predictions.question: 只加入 mτ_z 并打开中间交叉后，双值模型的两个 TRIM 端点会怎样？
choices: 端点仍有 Kramers 配对
predictions.explanation: mτ_z 破 G 但保 T，且物理自旋 T²=−I 不变。中间交叉与端点 Kramers 由不同条件保护。

predictions.question: 在 f_y=0.2 的螺旋模型切线上，仍画出相似交叉是否已经证明螺旋小群保护？

lessons.title: Construct Bloch representations from real-space half-translations
lessons.summary: First track the site permutation, then include intercell phases and spin rotations.

sections.title: Three-dimensional operations and invariant momenta
sections.text: The glide {m_y|a_x/2} reflects y, while the screw {C₂x|a_x/2} reverses y and z. Both preserve momentum along (f_x,0,0); at general k, test whether Rk−k is a reciprocal vector. Operations outside the little group map states to another momentum and cannot directly label the same band’s states.

sections.title: Periodic Bloch basis
sections.text: Within a cell, A lies at x=0 and B at x=a/2. A half translation sends A to B and B to A in the next cell. In the Fourier convention based on cell labels, the intercell term is exp(−ik_x), giving S=[[0,exp(−ik_x)],[1,0]]. Here k_x is in radians; the interface uses f_x=k_x/(2π).

sections.title: Single-valued versus double-valued representations
sections.text: For spinless states, G=S. For spin 1/2 use G=S⊗iσ_axis; choose axis=y for the glide and axis=x for the screw. A double spin rotation gives −I, introducing an extra i in the eigenvalues. This choice includes an explicit central-sign convention for  double group .

sections.title: Representation replay and periodic sewing
sections.text: Inspect S, G, G², and H frame by frame. Increasing k_x by 2π returns the matrix to itself, with sewing matrix I; continuously tracked positive and negative eigenvalue labels nevertheless exchange. This concerns the single-valuedness of labels and cannot be resolved by arbitrary line drawing or omitted phases.

lessons.title: Time reversal, partner switching and actual band crossings
lessons.summary: Connect double-valued endpoint Kramers conditions, glide labels, and intermediate band connectivity step by step.

sections.title: Endpoints and the antiunitary square
sections.text: Physical time reversal is T=(I⊗iσ_y)K, with T²=−I. Kramers' theorem applies at the same momentum only when −k is equivalent to k and the Hamiltonian preserves T. At a generic interior k point, T maps a state to −k and does not automatically imply a twofold degeneracy at the same point.

sections.title: The two endpoints pair states differently
sections.text: Double-valued labels at Γ are ±i, and T exchanges conjugate labels. At X the labels are ±1, and T partners share the same label. An isolated four-band set must switch partners between the endpoints. The calculation diagonalizes G within each degenerate energy block, rather than treating arbitrary numerical eigenvectors as G eigenstates.

sections.title: Obtain the crossing from the Hamiltonian
sections.text: Define A=(1+cos k)τ_x+sin k τ_y and B=sin k τ_x+(1−cos k)τ_y, and choose H₀=t A⊗I+λ B⊗σ_axis. This strictly periodic four-band model preserves G and T. For positive t and λ, the inner two bands cross at k_*=2 arctan(t/λ); every plotted point is an energy of this matrix.

sections.title: The spinless model and its material limitations
sections.text: In the single-valued model, the G labels at X are ±i. Time reversal T exchanges them and can enforce pairing, but T²=+I, so this is not spinful Kramers degeneracy. Experiments and theory on KHgSb provide material context for nonsymmorphic surface bands. This calculation uses only a minimal line model and does not reproduce measured parameters or the complete surface topology.

lessons.title: Minimal symmetry breaking, a gap along the entire line, and a subspace assignment
lessons.summary: Test protection with an actual perturbation, distinguishing a shifted crossing, a genuine gap and surviving endpoint pairing.

sections.title: A mass that preserves T and breaks G
sections.text: mτ_z⊗I anticommutes with H₀’s orbital off-diagonal terms, breaking G covariance while preserving T. Each massless branch becomes a massive square-root branch, giving a minimum direct gap 2|m| along the full line. Double-valued endpoint Kramers pairing survives. Common dispersion ε cos k shifts all energies at the same k together.

sections.title: Comparative experiment of preserving G and breaking T
sections.text: In the double-valued model, b I⊗σ_axis preserves G and breaks T. Small b may merely move a crossing, so the challenge uses sufficiently large b and supplies a positive gap lower bound for the whole line. The single-valued comparison term is b B(k), not an electronic Zeeman field. Gapping the original crossing position does not establish a gap along the entire path.

sections.title: group-subgroup relationship diagram
sections.text: The diagram shows the two specified constraints G and T and their removal, after quotienting translations and the double-group center. The label quotient has order 4, 2 or 1. Matrices still retain the actual G² translation phase and T² minus sign. This is not a full subgroup catalog of arbitrary three-dimensional space groups.

sections.title: Score by subspace
sections.text: Find every lowest-energy eigenvector at the selected k and submit them as matrix columns. At degeneracy, different numerical solvers may choose different bases; overall phases and internal unitary mixing are equivalent. Check dimension, orthogonal projector and invariance of the subspace under H rather than demanding entrywise-identical eigenvectors.

exercises.title: Derive glide eigenvalues from two sites
exercises.prompt: Use the double-valued glide preset and representation-construction replay to complete four derivation steps.

steps.prompt: Why does the intercell matrix element of S contain e^(−ik_x)?
steps.hint: B falls to the next unit cell after half translation.
choices: records Bloch phase across a unit cell
steps.explanation: The phase comes from an intercell displacement in real space. The spin-square factor enters independently in the next step.

steps.prompt: What is S² equal to when there is no spin?
choices: I is constant for all k
steps.explanation: Two site substitutions return to the original site type, while crossing a lattice period.

steps.prompt: After the double-valued spin factor squares to −I, what is G²?
steps.hint: Orbital and spin factors are multiplied.
steps.explanation: cannot lose the fractional translation phase, nor can it lose the negative sign of the spin 2π rotation.

steps.prompt: k_x→k_x+2π, how do the continuous label g₊ and the matrix G change?
steps.hint: Inspect the half-angle exponential and complete matrix separately.
choices: g₊ switches labels while G remains periodic
steps.explanation: Label switching of a single eigenvalue branch is not inconsistent with the periodic Bloch basis.

exercises.title: Derivation of intermediate crossovers from endpoint labels
exercises.prompt: holds m=b=0 and the transverse component is zero, first derive and then check the numerical energy bands.

steps.prompt: What do you get when the double-valued Γ terminal T acts on the +i tag?
steps.explanation: Members of one Kramers pair carry opposite purely imaginary G labels.

steps.prompt: What does Kramers partner carry for dual value X-side +1 tag?
steps.hint: The conjugate of real numbers is unchanged.
steps.explanation: With T symmetry and T²=−I, partners have equal energy; a real G label remains unchanged.

steps.prompt: t=λ>0, what is the internal crossover f_x?
spin-free X-point pairing be called a Kramers degeneracy of T²=−I?
steps.hint: first calculates the square of time reversal .
choices: No: T²=+I; the complex G labels must also be considered
Yes, as long as it can have crossover
steps.explanation: Single value T²=+I does not force pairing on its own; in X it swaps different G sectors that are conjugated to each other.

exercises.title: proves the gap and retains the correct degeneracy conclusion
exercises.prompt: Compare the unperturbed result with m=0.3 and complete the subspace assignment.

steps.prompt: How does mτ_z relate to the off-diagonal orbital structure of half translation?
steps.hint: τ_z anticommutes with τ_x and τ_y.
choices: destroys G, but does not destroy physical T
steps.explanation: G swaps A/B, τ_z distinguishes A/B; real and spin-independent τ_z preserves T.

steps.prompt: For m=0.3,b=0, what is the minimum middle direct gap along the entire Γ—X path?
steps.explanation: The upper and lower energy at the massless intersection is ±|m|, and the minimum direct gap across the entire line is 2|m|.

steps.prompt: The small Zeeman term causes a non-zero gap at the original intersection. Can the entire line be immediately declared insulated?
steps.hint: The intersection may move, and the direct gap and the indirect gap are different.
choices: No; check the entire path. Establishing a material insulator additionally requires the full Brillouin zone.
steps.explanation: challenge gives a full-line direct gap lower bound; this result is still not a global insulation proof for three-dimensional materials.

steps.prompt: The eigenvectors of two orthogonal bases of the same dimension are different one by one, but the projection matrices are the same. How should they be judged?
steps.hint: compares subspaces rather than choosing arbitrary bases.
choices: is regarded as the same correct subspace
only allows real numbers with overall positive sign
steps.explanation: The overall phase and the unitary within the subspace change of basis do not change the physical subspace; the dimensionality and H invariance also need to be checked.

cases.title: KHgSb: from glide-symmetric surface states to partner switching
cases.kind: KHgSb material background and minimal line model
cases.summary: Connect the intercell phases of Wyckoff sites, double-valued representations, and actual diagonalization. Compare the middle crossing and endpoint pairing at m=0 and m≠0.
cases.assumption: refers to material theory and experiment, but the current four-band parameters do not fit KHgSb; the topological index of the real sample is not announced based on this.
links: From Wyckoff sites to band representations

cases.title: Screw chain: the same translation phase, different rotation axes
cases.kind: On-axis line model of a three-dimensional twofold screw
cases.summary: Using a two-site chain as structural context, change the mirror lift's rotation axis y to screw axis x. Record eigenphases, endpoint pairing, and invariant-momentum conditions.
cases.assumption: This constructs a valid teaching representation of {C₂x|a_x/2}; it specifies neither a complete material space group nor a classification of every screw order.
links: space group and double group Classroom

cases.title: Alternating onsite potential: distinguish spatial-symmetry and time-reversal breaking
cases.kind: Model comparison: inequivalent sites and magnetic fields
cases.summary: Apply opposite onsite potentials to A/B or an axial magnetic field to the spin, and test G and T covariance separately. Use the full-line lower bound to complete the minimal symmetry-breaking challenge.
cases.assumption: m and b are explicit model parameters; the site potential is not automatically equivalent to some real structural distortion, nor does it output the full space group .
